newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco unleaded buyers, sellers far apart.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco unleaded buyers, sellers far apart.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline traders remained far apart on Monday in Chicago, with buyers and sellers playing a waiting game following a court decision expected to boost gasoline production in the region.

The spread between bid and ask prices widened to as much as three cents a gallon, with buyers and sellers both expressing little interest in narrowing the gap before the end of the current cycle, traders said.
"We're looking to buy, but there's no need to do anything before the 18th to 20th," one trader said, referring to the end of the next cycle.
Bids on Chicago unleaded were pegged at 6.25 cents a gallon over NYMEX December unleaded for prompt deliveries and 5.0 cents a gallon over the print for later deliveries.

But with Gulf coast unleaded talked 4.75/5.0 cents a gallon over the print, refiners would need a higher differential to cover transportation costs, and traders said perceptions of tight stocks had pushed the asking price on unleaded barrels in Chicago to as high as 8.25 cents a gallon over the print.

Few deals have been done since since Friday, when an Illinois judge cleared the way for Clark Refining and Marketing Co to restart two units at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island refinery, traders said.
Discussion also was muted after key Chicago players departed for the American Petroleum Institute annual convention in Washington, D.C.
Group Three unleaded firmed slightly to 4.25/4.50 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and was steady at 1.50/1.75 cents over for later deliveries.
Distillates were largely unchanged in late discussion.
